parsed.title: Workflow contract violation: fold-findings instructs manual script execution
parsed.detail: The SKILL.md states that on a freeze-batch, the loop 'stops and routes to `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`'. This contradicts the 'Review-end turn boundary' in review-change/SKILL.md and the general workflow contract that skills are user-invocable or composed by an orchestrator, not executed manually by the agent mid-turn. The agent should output a `→ Next:` block recommending the command, not execute it itself. Furthermore, fold-findings is a 'repair' skill; inserting a routing step that requires user confirmation (as per plan-feature/plan-fix docs) breaks the atomic 'repair' contract of the fold cycle.

parsed.title: Workflow contract violation: fold-findings references manual script execution
parsed.detail: Same defect as in SKILL.md. The reference doc states the loop 'stops and routes to `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`'. This is an operational instruction for the agent to run a script, which violates the separation of concerns where `workflow-status` or an orchestrator determines the next step, and skills report their state/next actions via `→ Next:` blocks.

parsed.title: Spec drift: Replan exemption logic order
parsed.detail: The 'Progressive loading' section lists step 4: 'Only when `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <NN>` prints `route: replan`: load the [replan contract]'. However, ROUTING.md (also in this slice) states under 'Replan exemption': 'Before the status gate, run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <NN>`'. The SKILL.md loading order (step 4) implies the replan contract is loaded *after* the standard routing steps (status gate, product-review gate), whereas ROUTING.md says it runs *before* the status gate to potentially skip it. The SKILL.md loading sequence contradicts the exemption logic described in ROUTING.md.

parsed.title: Spec drift: Replan exemption logic order
parsed.detail: Similar to plan-feature, SKILL.md lists the replan contract loading as step 7 (after planning preflight and phase contract). However, PLANNING_PROCESS.md (also in this slice) states under 'Replan detection': 'run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` first... A `route: replan` line means... load [the replan contract]'. The SKILL.md progressive loading order contradicts the 'first' execution requirement in the reference process doc.

parsed.title: Usage-docs: Incorrect invocation for replan route
parsed.detail: The doc states: 'run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` — its `route: replan` line names the planner... The planner re-cuts the plan... a fresh `/review-plan <unit>` passes, and only then `execute-phase` runs them.' This implies the reviewer should execute the router and the planner. However, `review-change`'s own Turn Contract (in SKILL.md) states: 'it never invokes `/fold-findings`, `/execute-phase`, `/plan-feature`, `/design-feature`...'. The reviewer should not run the planner; it should report the finding and let the user/orchestrator decide.

parsed.title: Usage-docs: Incorrect invocation for replan route
parsed.detail: The doc states: 'any finding routed replan-in-unit or owned by plan? → `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>` prints `route: replan`... the planner re-cuts the plan... a fresh `/review-plan <unit>` passes, then `/execute-phase <unit>`'. This instructs the reviewer to execute the entire replan and execution chain, which contradicts the `review-change` skill's boundary that it 'never invokes... `/execute-phase`... or edits code'.

parsed.title: Workflow contract violation: Triage executes router
parsed.detail: The diagram and text state: 'replan-in-unit runs `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`...'. Triage is a classification/decision skill. It should not execute the router or the planner. It should report the finding and recommend the next step (e.g., `→ Next: /plan-feature <unit>` after router confirms replan). Executing the router here bypasses the orchestrator's state management.

parsed.title: Workflow contract violation: Triage process executes router
parsed.detail: Same as above. The process doc instructs: 'Run `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit>`... and the fresh `/review-plan <unit>` that must pass before execution.' Triage should not run the review plan. It should triage the finding and hand off.
